entities.evidence: וּלְאָדָם uses the personal name Adam without the article. It refers to the man who has just named the animals, and the source tag identifies him as Adam@Gen.2.19.

review.translation: [And|0] [the man|1] [gave|0] [names|2] [to all|3] [the livestock|4] [and to the bird|5]{s} [of|5] [the sky|6] [and to every|7] [wild animal of|8] [the field|9], [but for Adam|10] [he did|12] [not|11] [find|12] [a helper|13] [corresponding to him|14].

analysis.evidence: הָאָדָם is the subject, שֵׁמוֹת (“names”) is the direct object, and the phrases beginning with לְ identify the animals to which the man gave names.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא הָאָדָם שֵׁמוֹת, “the man gave names,” הָאָדָם is the definite subject of the singular verb וַיִּקְרָא. It identifies the individual who names the animals.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular common noun in the absolute state.

draft.change: Clarify the first Hebrew noun sense in shem to include the animals in its defining passage, and explain the plural in the verse evidence.
draft.definition: A name by which a person or creature is called.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:20 uses שֵׁמוֹת for the names the man gives the animals.

patch.value: Whatever the man calls each creature is its name, שְׁמוֹ. The plural שֵׁמוֹת gathers the names he gives the livestock, birds, and wild animals.
name by which a person or creature is called

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא הָאָדָם שֵׁמוֹת, the man is the subject and שֵׁמוֹת is the direct object. The following לְ phrases identify the livestock, birds, and wild animals to which he gave names.
analysis.morphology: Masculine common noun, plural absolute, with the plural ending ־וֹת.
analysis.sense: A name by which a creature is called.

analysis.evidence: In לְכָל הַבְּהֵמָה, כָל quantifies the definite collective noun הַבְּהֵמָה. The man gave names “to all the livestock.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed preposition לְ.

analysis.evidence: The man gives names to לְכָל הַבְּהֵמָה, ‘all the livestock’. The verse lists the birds of the heavens and the wild animals of the field separately, supporting the domestic-animal sense.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In וּלְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, ‘and to the birds of the sky’, הַשָּׁמַיִם completes the construct phrase. The man gives names to the birds as a group alongside the livestock and the wild animals.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ + preposition לְ־ ‘to’ + masculine singular construct noun עוֹף, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In וּלְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, “and to the birds of the sky,” the sky identifies the birds’ habitat, just as the field identifies the habitat of the animals in חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: In וּלְכֹל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה, כֹל quantifies the singular חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה “beast of the field.” The man gave names to every such animal.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ “and” + preposition לְ־ “to” + masculine singular construct noun כֹל.

analysis.evidence: חַיַּת stands in construct with הַשָּׂדֶה. The phrase וּלְכֹל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה means “and to every wild animal of the field,” completing the list after the livestock and the birds of the sky.
analysis.sense: wild beast, beast of the field

analysis.evidence: In חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה, “beast of the field,” הַשָּׂדֶה names the habitat of wild animals, just as הַשָּׁמַיִם names the habitat of birds in עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: open country, the land outside town and house

analysis.evidence: The verse opens with הָאָדָם (“the man”) naming the animals. In וּלְאָדָם, the pointing לְ־ shows that the name has no article. The clause singles out Adam as the one for whom no corresponding helper was found, the same bearer identified as Adam@Gen.2.19.
analysis.morphology: וּ־ (conjunction, here adversative) + לְ־ (preposition, “for”) + אָדָם (masculine singular personal name, absolute, without the article)

analysis.evidence: לֹא negates the perfect verb מָצָא ‘found’. The clause reports that he did not find a helper corresponding to Adam.
analysis.morphology: Negative particle without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: לֹא negates מָצָא, and עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ is its direct object. The clause reads “for the man he found no helper corresponding to him.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עֵזֶר is the object of מָצָא, “found.” כְּנֶגְדּוֹ describes the helper as corresponding to the man. Among the animals he named, he found no such helper.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: a helper, one who is help

analysis.evidence: כְּנֶגְדּוֹ qualifies עֵזֶר ‘helper’, and the suffix refers to the man. After naming the animals, he found no helper who corresponded to him.
analysis.morphology: Preposition נֶגֶד with prefixed כְּ ‘as, like’ and third-person masculine singular suffix ־וֹ ‘him’.
analysis.sense: (כְּנֶגְדּוֹ) as in front of him: corresponding to him, his counterpart
